name: Maize Ear Rot
description: A fungal disease complex that rots maize ears, reducing grain yield and quality. Some ear rot fungi produce mycotoxins (fumonisins, aflatoxins) that are hazardous to human and livestock health. It is favored by wet conditions during silking and grain fill.
symptoms: Pinkish-white or greenish mold on kernels
Kernels appearing discolored, shriveled, or decayed
Rot starting from ear tip and progressing downward
Premature husk death and ear drooping
Ears may show scattered infected kernels among healthy ones
causes: Fusarium verticillioides, Aspergillus flavus, Gibberella zeae fungi
Wet weather during silking and grain fill
Insect damage to ears creating entry points
Bird damage opening ears to fungal infection
Continuous maize cropping with infected residue
treatments: No effective in-season treatment once ear rot develops
Harvest infected fields early and separately
Dry harvested grain to below 15% moisture immediately
Sort and remove visibly infected kernels before storage
prevention: Plant hybrids with good husk cover and ear rot resistance
Control insect pests (corn earworm, stalk borer)
Avoid high plant densities that increase humidity
Harvest promptly at maturity and dry grain quickly
Practice crop rotation with non-cereal crops
Use balanced fertilization — avoid excess nitrogen
